scope: This slice checks C11 atomic types and source operations. It retains AtomicLoad conversions and single AtomicAccess store/read-modify-write plans with sequentially consistent C semantics. Initializers preserve atomic storage types but do not imply atomic stores.

The native operations were compiled/executed by GCC and Clang at O0/O2 on x86_64 Linux. They establish compiler behavior and check matching semantic acceptance/retention; Toucan does not generate atomic machine code or implement a concurrent memory model.

The compiler integration test checks 27 types with three size/alignment/offset assertions each across five selected profiles. The two GNU Linux profiles use the native Linux GCC driver for this shared LP64 layout matrix; this does not constitute native ARM execution. Darwin/MSVC use Clang cross-target LLVM compilation.

Exploratory constraints preserve compiler diagnostics, including extensions and rejected cases. They are research inputs, not a claim that every accepted compiler extension is supported. The checked integration test defines the supported source matrix and explicit diagnostics.

Atomic storage layout is profile-specific: GNU raises alignment for power-of-two objects at most16bytes; Clang rounds objects at most16bytes to a power of two. No lock-free guarantee follows. Increased scalar typedef alignment survives under GNU but Clang atomic storage may reduce it; ordinary loaded values retain their typedef alignment.

Unpromoted aligned-typedef arithmetic retains the existing explicit diagnostic, including through Atomic, instead of inventing observable typeof alignment. Atomic loads in GNU overflow predicates remain observable, so those third operands cannot become integer constant expressions.

Clang atomic rvalues retain Atomic; GNU cast and function-return values drop it. Clang ignores atomic qualifiers inside array parameter brackets; direct atomic pointer parameters remain distinct. GNU incomplete atomic pointees can be represented but incomplete/void atomic storage has no layout.

Direct atomic aggregate member access is diagnosed. Selected atomic bindings require a proved Rust storage and call-ABI representation; ordinary aggregate emission is unsafe because atomic and non-atomic record call conventions differ.

The unchanged GCC13 stdatomic.h smoke currently stops at undefined predefined __INT_LEAST8_TYPE__ and related least/fast type names. GNU __auto_type macro support and Clang __c11_atomic_* integration remain separate work. Native compiler acceptance of that smoke is preserved without claiming Toucan accepts it.

The four ordinary semantic allocation samples exactly match1dd52e3. Atomic constructor walks and retained type walks are bounded; the constructor node/depth regression rejects a2000-alias chain before unbounded expansion. Twelve seed/profile checks validate retained arena edges; this report does not claim a new sanitizer campaign.

The normal-source and retained-source outcomes are compared by full Debug translation-unit equality in every focused semantic test. Native graph/effect tests run independently of optional binding generation.
